messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we've got an incident where a model-level flag (enable_attention_experiment) is true for a canary, but the org-level flag is false. Is the intended precedence org > project > route > model or the other way? Seeing mixed behavior in prod canaries.

Leo: Short answer: org-level should be the ceiling (highest priority) unless the org explicitly marks that flag as overridable. Longer answer below. :eyes:

Sasha: I thought lower scopes (route/model) win over higher ones. Can we get the canonical order?

Tomas: Canonical resolution we use is: default -> org -> project -> route -> model, where later (narrower) scope can override wider scope only if the flag is not locked at a higher scope. In practice: org can set lock: true which prevents any downstream override.

Maya: Helpful. How is "lock" expressed in config? Example pls.

Tomas: Example config snippet we use in the flag service (pseudo-yaml):

```yaml
flags:
  enable_attention_experiment:
    default: false
    org:
      value: false
      locked: true   # if locked, no lower-scope overrides allowed
    project:
      billing_team: {}
    route:
      /search/fast:
        value: true  # would normally override, but org.locked blocks it
    model:
      gpt-lite-1: { value: true }
```

Sasha: So locked=true on org blocks the route/model true. If org has locked=false but value=false, route/model true can win?

Leo: Yes. If org.locked is false (or omitted), narrower scopes may override. Also remember we have a allowlist/guardrail pattern: org can include overridable_scopes (e.g., projects or routes allowed to override even if default disallows).

Anya: Edge cases: what if a scope sets value: null? We treat null as "inherit" and continue up the chain. Also explicit false beats inherit/undefined.

Maya: We're seeing a case where route has value=true but model has no entry; route wins as expected. But prod telemetry showed traffic still using org=false. Could be old cache or incorrect evaluation path.

FlagBot: FlagService: evaluated enable_attention_experiment for request id=abc123, resolved_scope=org, value=false (org.locked=true)

Leo: If FlagService logs resolved_scope=org then override didn't apply. Two likely causes: 1) org.locked=true or 2) the route key didn't match because route naming changed (e.g., "/search/fast" vs "/search-fast").

Sasha: Also check the rollout guardrails: if the route-level flag is part of a canary audience, we require explicit canary config. Example of canary stanza: 

```json
{
  "route": "/search/fast",
  "overrides": {
    "enable_attention_experiment": {
      "value": true,
      "canary": {
        "pct": 5,
        "audience": "internal-beta"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
If canary is missing but the route declares value:true, the platform will downgrade to resolved_scope=org for safety when guardrails are active. That's another reason for seeing org-level resolution.

Maya: Great point. I'll check the route config for canary fields.

Tomas: Ops checklist: 1) check FlagService audit log for resolved_scope, 2) confirm org.locked flag, 3) confirm route key exact match, 4) check canary stanza and audience membership, 5) clear flag-service cache if recent change.

Anya: Tests to add: unit test for null inheritance, integration test where org.locked=false but route override succeeds, and a guardrail test that forces downgrade when canary missing.

Maya: I'll open a tiny PR with tests and the failing trace attached. Assigning to @Leo for review. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/flags-service/pull/482 :point_right:

Leo: Thanks — will review tomorrow. If it's a config mismatch we can patch without deploy. If it's codepath, we'll triage severity. :thumbsup:

Sasha: One more note — update the docs page under /docs/flags/scope-resolution to include the locked/overridable examples and the canary fallback behavior.

Maya: Will do. Adding to my checklist. Thanks all. :rocket:
